thread.title: Man accused of shooting girlfriend in Urbana found fit to stand trial - NewsBreak

author: Molly Sweeney
title: Man accused of shooting girlfriend in Urbana found fit to stand trial - NewsBreak
text:
By Molly Sweeney ,
5 hours ago
CHAMPAIGN COUNTY, Ill. (WCIA) -- The Urbana man accused of shooting his girlfriend last year has been found fit to stand trial.
Court records show Noah Allen appeared in court for a fitness hearing on Thursday, Nov. 5. The court considered "all of the reports, including the expert opinion(s) and bases for the opinion(s), the court's observations of the defendant in court, and all relevant evidence..." to make its ruling, records show.
Suspect in Urbana shooting facing three charges, up to 55 years in prison Allen is charged with attempted murder, aggravated battery with a firearm and possession of a firearm by a repeat felon. He's accused of shooting his 21-year-old girlfriend across the street from Urbana Middle School on Oct. 7, 2025 .
Before going into surgery, the victim told police she and Allen were arguing because Allen was drunk, and that during their argument he tried forcing her into a car. She also told police this was not the first time Allen had threatened her with a gun.
Since the shooting, there have been multiple questions about Allen's competency. In January of 2026, he was found fit to stand trial or enter a plea . But several months later, in April, the court found him unfit and placed him in the custody of the Illinois Department of Human Services.
How that he has been found fit, Allen is scheduled to appear in court again for a pre-trial conference on Dec. 1.
